notes: Identity checked independently from the supplied text: title What Counts as a Choice? U.S. Americans Are More Likely Than Indians to Construe Actions as Choices; authors Krishna Savani, Hazel Rose Markus, N.V.R. Naidu, Satishchandra Kumar, and Neha Berlia; DOI 10.1177/0956797609359908; Psychological Science 21(3), 391–398 (2010). This is the primary research article, with five studies, methods, results, figures, and references, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied. Only assigned original-side fields were examined; other fields are placeholders. Matched by the explicitly named condition contrast and dependent variable, not numerical agreement or row order. The article also reports a culture main effect (d = 0.55), a Culture × Condition interaction (F = 5.69), and a cultural simple effect within the choice condition (d = 1.03); these answer different contrasts. Retained the printed d and exact p = .01 from the same condition main-effect test. Participant counts in Method are recruitment counts; no final analytic N is explicitly supplied.
